title: Dominant multiplication from finitely many Cartan subgroups
statement:
Let $k$ be an infinite field [def-weil-field], and let $G$ be a smooth [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], geometrically connected [def-weil-connected-scheme], affine group scheme [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$. Tori and maximal tori mean [def-sfb-tori-multiplicative-type, def-sfb-reductive-torus-centralizer-terminology]. For a closed torus $T\subseteq G$, write $C_G(T)$ for the smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup representing the centralizer functor [lem-sfb-torus-centralizer-smooth-connected]: its $A$-points commute with every point of $T$ after every commutative $A$-algebra extension. There are an integer $m\geq1$ and maximal $k$-tori $T_1,\ldots,T_m\subseteq G$ for which the multiplication morphism
$$\mu:C_G(T_1)\times_k\cdots\times_k C_G(T_m)\longrightarrow G,\qquad(c_1,\ldots,c_m)\longmapsto c_1\cdots c_m$$
has dense image on underlying Zariski topological spaces. In particular every nonempty Zariski open subset of $G$ has nonempty inverse image under $\mu$. The trivial group is allowed; no reductivity or perfectness assumption is made.

source.place: Theorem 17.91, printed p.381, and the dominant-product assertion in the proof of Corollary 17.92, printed p.382; Cartan subgroups are centralizers of maximal tori (17.43--17.44 and p.381).

proof.text: By [lem-sfb-cartan-subgroups-generate], the set $I$ of maximal $k$-tori in $G$ is nonempty, and a closed $k$-subgroup containing $C_G(T)$ for every $T\in I$ must be $G$. For each $T\in I$ put $H_T=C_G(T)$. By [lem-sfb-torus-centralizer-smooth-connected], each $H_T$ is a smooth geometrically connected closed subgroup of $G$; as a closed subgroup of the affine finite-type scheme $G$, it is affine of finite type. Thus this family satisfies the generation and connectedness hypotheses of the general finite-word lemma. These assertions hold over the original field $k$; no rational-point density or passage to a perfect field is used.

source.place: Theorem 17.91, printed p.381; Cartan-subgroup paragraph preceding Proposition 17.90.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-connected-subgroups-finite-word] to the nonempty family $(H_T)_{T\in I}$ from step 1. It gives $m\geq1$ and indices $T_1,\ldots,T_m\in I$ such that the ordered multiplication of the $H_{T_j}$ has dense image. Substituting $H_{T_j}=C_G(T_j)$ gives exactly the displayed morphism $\mu$ of the statement, with the indicated order of factors. Repetitions are allowed, so no distinctness assumption on the tori is needed. For the trivial group the trivial rank-zero torus is maximal and its centralizer is the group itself; a single factor gives the identity morphism, consistent with the lemma's $m\geq1$ conclusion.

source.place: Proof of Corollary 17.92, printed p.382, finite dominant product before the unirationality argument.

proof.text: If $U\subseteq G$ is nonempty and Zariski open and $\mu^{-1}(U)$ were empty, the image of $\mu$ would be contained in the closed set $G\setminus U$. Its closure would then also be contained in that set, contradicting the density proved in step 2. Hence $\mu^{-1}(U)$ is nonempty.

source.place: Elementary consequence of dominance in the proof of Corollary 17.92, printed p.382.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 17.91 and proof of Corollary 17.92, printed pp.381-382; finite-word supporting lemma made explicit.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q57-901e06f9e (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, both new nodes and the cited statements. Against Milne iAG2017: the Cartan-subgroup paragraph before 17.90 and Theorem 17.91 on p.381 (the item assumes k infinite, the case Milne proves; the finite-field case is only cited), Corollary 17.92 and Theorem 17.93 on p.382, Theorem 17.82 and Corollary 17.83 on p.379, and section 2h on generated subgroups (2.46-2.53). Steps: step 1 takes nonemptiness of the maximal tori and generation from lem-sfb-cartan-subgroups-generate, and takes smoothness and geometric connectedness of C_G(T) from lem-sfb-torus-centralizer-smooth-connected; its full statement covers any torus. Step 2 meets every hypothesis of lem-sfb-connected-subgroups-finite-word, and the substitution H_T = C_G(T) gives exactly the item's map. Step 3 is elementary. The generation node is Milne 17.91 with generation in the smallest-subgroup sense, so the containing subgroup H may be non-reduced. I checked the finite-word node is true by a maximal-dimension word-closure argument with descent to k, and tested both nodes on the trivial group, G_a, tori, GL_2, the two axes in G_a^2, and SL_2 with U+ and U- (U+U-U+ is dense, so repetition is needed and allowed). Neither node restates the item. My duplicate search found only nearby nodes (affine-pointed-map-generated-subgroup, pointed-word-kernel-stabilization, derived-commutator-word, smooth-subgroup-tangent-generation, semisimple-centralizer-reduction), none of which states either lemma. Batch-5 finding: lem-trf-smooth-at-point-fibre-criterion, reached through the torus-centralizer node, is Stacks 01V9, the fibrewise smoothness criterion. It is general algebraic geometry, not the trace formula, Poincare duality or a step of their proofs, and the item already cited the centralizer node on the base, so I did not return for it. Minor remark, not repaired: 'geometrically connected' cites only def-weil-connected-scheme, the same convention as the base item.
